title: HEARTWOOD / REVEAL THE INNER VALUE
core_formula: found mass -> identify hidden volume -> remove material -> insert function into the void -> preserve provenance -> collectible object
secondary_lesson: LET THE MATERIAL FRAME THE FUNCTION.
summary: A found wood mass is opened from within so a light source can occupy the revealed void, preserving provenance while transforming the object into a collectible lamp.
learn: Ask what is inside the material and what can be opened, carved or freed.
Treat empty space as active design material.
Place function inside the found object instead of beside it.
Removing material can be more powerful than adding decoration.
Preserve provenance rather than erasing the past.
Function can help reveal the beauty of material.
Subtractive transformation can create collectible value from familiar mass.
avoid: tree stumps as a default answer
Edison bulbs as the only light source
one vertical slit as a fixed composition
dark bark plus amber glow as mandatory styling
wooden bases as a permanent requirement
rustic lamps as the only direction
failure_modes: the wood is over-processed and loses provenance
the cavity feels generic rather than discovered from the material
the lamp looks like ordinary rustic decor instead of a considered collectible
the light source feels glued on rather than integrated into the void
too much refinement erases the contrast between outer bark and inner light
the base and wiring distract from the core subtractive transformation
